issuing_body: Minnesota District Court, Hennepin County, Fourth Judicial District
title: Order for Judgment, Minnesota Department of Education v. Emadeldin Ibrahim, Court File No. 27-CV-22-13107
supports: The court ordered judgment for the Minnesota Department of Education against Emadeldin Ibrahim in the amount of $2,481,310.08 plus prejudgment interest.
The jury's April 23, 2026 unanimous verdict found Ibrahim knowingly submitted 90,636 false or fraudulent claims in 2021 under the Minnesota False Claims Act.
The court states MDE incurred $188,350.84 in damages from Ibrahim's false claims submitted through the At-Risk Afterschool Meal component of CACFP.
The court trebled compensatory damages to $565,052.52 under Minn. Stat. § 15C.02(a).
The court imposed a $1,695,157.56 civil penalty, applying a 9:1 ratio to the $188,350.84 compensatory damages after considering the Excessive Fines Clause and Minnesota/Eighth Circuit authority.
The court awarded $220,700 in attorneys' fees and $400 in court costs, totaling $221,100 in fees/costs.
The order states the court held $106,978.10 previously deposited by Wells Fargo and that a separate order releasing those funds to MDE would issue after entry of judgment.

money.notes: Order for judgment amount excluding prejudgment interest to be calculated separately.
Jury-found MDE damages from false claims; this amount is included in the treble-damages calculation and must not be added again to the total judgment.
Three times the $188,350.84 compensatory damages; component of the total judgment.
Component of the total judgment: $220,700 attorneys' fees + $400 court costs.
Court states these funds were already held and a separate release order to MDE would issue; do not treat the full $2.48M judgment as collected.

important_qualifications: This is a civil Minnesota False Claims Act adjudication, not a criminal conviction.
The total judgment components are nested and must not be summed on top of the $2,481,310.08 total.
Judgment entered is not the same as judgment collected. The order itself identifies only $106,978.10 as funds already held by the court pending release, not full satisfaction of the judgment.
This CACFP case is separate from Feeding Our Future unless a source establishes a direct case relationship.
